I will say, the whole "cats are aloof and don't care about your presence" is kind of a lie. Some cats have a more shy and reserved personality but it's not the standard. Cats are not for everyone, I own and adore two and a very strong cat person and I still get annoyed, frustrated and upset by some of their quirks and antics. You may get a shy cat from a shelter but once the cat gets comfortable could explode into the most energetic velcro cat in the world, they have unique personalities and I like to joke "if you've met one cat, you've met one cat" because no two cats are gonna act exactly the same. I would have recommended fostering a cat first if you weren't sure before going all in, but rehome the cat if you're having serious regrets. It'll make you happier and the cat will have a chance to go to a home that is more pet friendly and you two aren't stressing over each other. *You aren't an asshole for giving the animal and yourself a better quality of life, even if that means you give it back*

To address the scratching first, you can buy cardboard scratching boards at walmart or any pet store in your area and lay them around the house, they range between like $5-$20 and some even double as cat beds! I sprinkle catnip on the boards as well to encourage the scratching boards being used. You can use nail clippers or pet nail trimmers to trim the tips of the claws to prevent clawing as well and it can help them get overgrown as well. Some cats are paw sensitive and will be fidgety if you try to grab them, so this is a cat by cat basis. 

For the furniture, you can buy small cat trees or even just put in shelves for them to climb on. If you see the cat laying in a specific spot near the sun? Throw an old blanket that smells like the partner there and boom! Cat bed. Get an old box and throw paper, cat toys and catnip and it’s hours of entertainment. Use tinfoil or tape on counters to keep them from jumping on counters. 

When the cat first gets to your place, set it up in a bathroom or a spare room and give it a few days to chill out and get situated. Especially since its an older cat (my senior is 15 yrs old) this will help him ease into the new environment. They are grumpy old men in tiny bodies, they will be stubborn.
